column37:
The most important thing that we found
is that you can't run it remotely., There is no way that someone sitting
in New York can tell you what, a fan in Amsterdam wants out of
their connection to your team., You got to be there., And a lot of times you're looking for
the people who are already into it., If you're the Packers and you want
to build a large fan base in Germany,, you're like, go find the Packers fans
in Germany, not just the expats, but the, German locals who have somehow found
an affinity for the team and start to, talk to them about why and how, and
you start to build around those people., I don't think there's, The sort of shotgun approach of fan
acquisition, we just haven't seen, anyone have a ton of success with,
including professional sports leagues., I think you get the most bang
for the buck when you're doing
the very grassroots fan-to-fan., Like, if you see a fan on social
media who is routinely liking
your stuff or interacting or, creating content, you want to
reach out to them and talk to them
and bring them into the fold, and use them to help bring other
fans in as a model for what
building fandom can look like., And a lot of people look at that and
they're like, well, that doesn't scale., And it's like,, Well, it does in the first six months to two
years as you're building the fan base, but, the whole idea is to turn that building,
that growing fan base into a flywheel that, no longer requires you to do those things
because the fan base is doing it themselves.
